case_name: Padmja Sharma vs Ratan Lal And Anr.

parties.respondent_defendant: Ratan Lal And Anr., husband and another

facts_of_case: Petitioner filed a divorce petition under Section 13 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. She moved an application to frame an issue regarding property belonging jointly to both parties. The trial court rejected her prayer.

legal_principles.principle: The Court will not review the findings of fact reached by inferior Courts.
legal_principles.held: Thus, the Court will not review the findings in of fact reached by the inferior Courts.
cited_cases: Satyanarayan Laxminarayan Hegde and Ors. v. Mallikerjun Bhavanappa Tirumala, AIR 1960 SC 137
K..K. Shrivastava etc. v. Bhupendra Kumar Jain and Ors., AIR 1977 SC 1703

legal_principles.principle: The Court should not exercise its powers under Article 227 of the Constitution for purposes of correcting mere errors.
legal_principles.held: This power is to be exercised most sparingly and only in appropriate cases in order to keep the Subordinate Courts within the bounds of their authority and not for correcting mere errors.
cited_cases: India Pipe Fitting Co. v. Fakruddtn M.A. Baker and Anr., AIR 1978 SC 45

legal_principles.principle: Interlocutory orders cannot be the subject matter of an appeal under Section 19 of the Family Courts Act.
legal_principles.held: In my view, interlocutory orders cannot be the subject matter of an appeal under Section 19 of the Family Courts Act but these orders can be challenged alongwith final order in the case and merely because they cannot be challenged at the interlocutory stage it would not mean that a writ petition should be entertained for quashing the order of the subordinate Court.

legal_principles.principle: The Court should not exercise its powers under Article 227 of the Constitution for purposes of correcting an error apparent on the face of record.
legal_principles.held: However, even if it may be said that this Court should exercise its powers under Article 227 of the Constitution for purposes of correcting an error apparent on the face of record, it may be looked into whether there is error apparent on the face of the record which requires correction by a writ of certiorari.
keywords: error apparent on the face of record

outcome.final_order: The final order was that the trial court's decision rejecting the petitioner's application was upheld.
